$comment: Something an office owes, because of the position it holds. A duty is always owed to somebody — that is what makes it a duty and not merely a good idea. Whoever it is owed to holds the matching claim: the duty and the claim are one fact read from two sides, so you cannot make a duty without also making someone who can hold you to it. A duty stands. It passes whole to whoever holds the office next, and it does not finish — tasks are raised against it, and each of those finishes. Duty is the root of the deontic terms: deon is that which is binding, and liberty, deontic-power and deontic-immunity are all named against it.

name.$comment: What the duty is called, as it is said: 'commissioning an office'.

authority.$comment: What binds you to it — a charter, a contract, a law, a custom. Names an authority and must resolve to one. Something holding the power to bind you has to have bound you, or you are not bound.

work.$comment: The work that is owed. Names a work and must resolve to one: an obligation to do something nobody has defined is an obligation nobody can meet.

claim.$comment: Who holds the claim on you — the other side of this same fact. A duty owed to nobody is not a duty: no one can hold you to it, and nothing is wronged when you fail.

skills.$comment: The skills that discharge it. Each names a skill and must resolve to one. A duty no skill can discharge is a wish.

delegation.$comment: Whether another may be authorised to do it for you. Even where they may, the answering-for stays with you: delegation hands out the doing, never the accountability.

$comment-absences: No holder or bearer: a duty passes whole to whoever holds the office next, and it cannot do that if it names who is sitting there now. The office's deontic profile is where the holder enters. No goal and no acceptance conditions: those belong to a task, which is raised against this duty and then ends. Conditions written onto a standing duty are stale the day after, and a duty is not the sort of thing that finishes. No discharged key: whether it has been discharged is a readout — run the goals of the tasks raised against it. No status: duties are not retired, the offices bearing them are.
